summary: RANK assigns the same rank to peer rows with equal window-order values.
documentation: RANK assigns the same rank to peer rows with equal window-order values. After a tie it leaves gaps, so two rows tied for first make the next rank three. A separate output ordering can make tied rows deterministic without breaking the peer groups.
inputs: scores(id INTEGER, score INTEGER NOT NULL).
returns: id, score and placement, ordered by score descending then id.
caution: Adding id to the window ORDER BY would break score ties. Use id only in the final presentation order.
scenarios: Create competition rankings for a local leaderboard.
Show tied bid positions without inventing a tie-break winner.
Rank review priorities while preserving equal scores.
title: Rank with competition gaps
problem: Return id, score and RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS placement. Present rows by score DESC, id ASC. Equal scores share rank, and later ranks contain gaps.
goal: Use RANK() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Window ranking and final row sorting serve different purposes.
